title: Handoff to delivery and customer success
nav: 5. Handoff to delivery and customer success
objective: Identify what CS needs from a presale ROI estimate.
clearance: Rewritten draft; pending SME and partner clearance

blocks.x: A good handoff means delivery and customer success don't have to restart discovery. The receiving owners also get what they need to prove value later.

items: The business problem, the sponsor, and the champion.
The prioritized workflows, with current and future maps.
The scope, including exclusions, unverified capabilities, and customer obligations.

blocks.x: What customer success needs from the value model
Glean's Value Playbook calls launching without a baseline the number one measurement failure. Customer success and value owners need:

items: The baseline period, or the plan to create a baseline.
Evidence labels, plus the recapture and reallocation assumptions.
A review cadence and a named, accountable value owner.

blocks.x: The receiving owner must accept the handoff explicitly. Record any unresolved dependencies and risks.

blocks.label: Boundary
blocks.x: Don't hand over an aspirational future-state diagram as an implementation commitment.
Customer success inherits the value model. Hand it over with its assumptions, not just its headline.

blocks.title: Value handoff to customer success
blocks.alt: A four-step handoff of the value model: share the metric cards and baselines, explain the assumptions and evidence levels, agree the measurement cadence, and confirm acceptance by the delivery and customer success owners.

items.label: Acceptance
items.detail: Delivery and CS confirm they own it

practice.x: List what customer success needs from a pre-sales ROI estimate.

worked.x: Metric definitions, the baseline period, the cohort, targets, data owners, evidence labels, the recapture and reallocation assumptions, costs, attribution caveats, a review cadence, and a named, accountable value owner who accepts the handoff.
